points: Issues: appointing/dismissing CMs, ordinances, reserving bills.
Populism is a dysfunction; jumbo ministry is a coalition demerit.

POL-9.3.2-Q19.lead: Regional parties are key coalition partners at the Centre.
points: Statement 1 is a positive role; statement 2 a dysfunction.
Since 1989 they have often acted as king-makers.

POL-9.3.2-Q20.lead: Widening voter choice is listed as a positive role.
points: The six dysfunctions include regionalism, '-isms', disputes, corruption, populism, coalition pressure.

POL-9.3.2-Q21.lead: Coalitio literally means to grow together.
points: Power-sharing and compromise are features, not the literal meaning.

POL-9.3.2-Q22.lead: Ogg structural; Robertson majority gap; Sahni multi-party.
points: Ghai: parties unite to exercise power on a common agenda.

POL-9.3.2-Q23.lead: Agreement in advance is why voters get a clear choice.
points: Post-poll alliances form after results, mainly to cross the majority mark.

POL-9.3.2-Q24.lead: Support gathered after results = post-poll alliance.
points: TVK won 108 of 234 seats; majority is 118.
It was not a single-party majority, so not one-party dominance.

POL-9.3.2-Q25.lead: Compromise is central; rigid ideology has no room.
points: Other features: temporary conjunction of interests, dynamism, power as the goal.

POL-9.3.2-Q26.lead: Coalitions rest on a temporary conjunction of interests.
points: Statement 1 is wrong: the alliance lasts only while interests overlap.

POL-9.3.2-Q27.lead: CPI, DMK and some small parties backed it from outside.
points: Congress(O) was the breakaway rival faction.
BJP (1980) and TDP (1982) did not exist then.
Congress regained a majority in 1971.

POL-9.3.2-Q28.lead: Janata Party government 1977–79 under Morarji Desai.
points: Charan Singh followed in 1979–80.
V.P. Singh led the National Front in 1989.
Deve Gowda led the United Front in 1996.

POL-9.3.2-Q29.lead: 1979 Charan Singh, 1989 V.P. Singh, 1990 Chandra Shekhar, 1997 Gujral.
points: Gujral succeeded Deve Gowda within the United Front (1996–98).

POL-9.3.2-Q30.lead: Congress won majorities again in 1980 and 1984.
points: In 2014 a single party (BJP) again won a majority.

POL-9.3.2-Q31.lead: BJP+Left backed V.P. Singh; Congress backed Chandra Shekhar; Left backed UPA-I.
points: Congress(I) also backed Charan Singh from outside in 1979.

POL-9.3.2-Q32.lead: Dependence on regional partners makes the Centre federal-minded.
points: Other merits: representativeness, consensus, checks on despotism.

POL-9.3.2-Q33.lead: Partners' coordination committee undermines the Cabinet.
points: Cabinet Secretariat assists the Cabinet; it is not a party body.
NITI Aayog and the Inter-State Council are governmental bodies.
The 91st Amendment (2003) later capped the ministry at 15% of Lok Sabha strength.

POL-9.3.2-Q35.lead: Consensus is a merit of coalitions.
points: Instability, king-makers and diffused responsibility are listed demerits.
The PM's pre-eminence is also curtailed.

POL-9.3.2-Q36.lead: BJP won 240, below the 272 majority mark.
points: 293 was the NDA total.
303 was BJP's 2019 tally.
272 is the majority mark in a 543-member House.
Shiv Sena was founded by Bal Thackeray; AIADMK by MGR; AGP by P.K. Mahanta.

POL-9.3.2-Q39.lead: KCR founded TRS in 2001; renamed BRS in 2022.
points: Jagan founded YSRCP in 2011.
Naidu leads TDP; Revanth Reddy is the Congress CM of Telangana.

POL-9.3.2-Q40.lead: All three dates and founders are correct.
points: P.A. Sangma co-founded NCP and later founded NPP.
AAP was founded by Arvind Kejriwal.

POL-9.3.2-Q42.lead: Congress under Revanth Reddy since December 2023.
points: TDP leads the AP government, not Telangana.
BJP and AIMIM are opposition parties in Telangana.
N. Chandrababu Naidu became CM in 2024.
YSRCP emerged from the Congress in 2011.

POL-9.3.2-Q44.lead: TVK is built around actor-leader Vijay.
points: It did not split from any national party.
It won 108 of 234 seats — first non-Dravidian lead since the 1960s.

POL-9.3.2-Q45.lead: Dependence on one leader explains their short life.
points: GBK notes exceptions; examples: LJP, AIADMK, NTR-TDP.

POL-9.4.1-Q02.lead: A is true; the Order was issued by the ECI, not Parliament.

head: Statement
Verdict
rows: A. ECI acts as court in symbol disputes

points: It was issued under Art 324 with the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961.
Dispute settlement is the ECI's quasi-judicial function.
Parties are national, state or registered-unrecognised.

POL-9.4.1-Q04.lead: All three are independent routes to national status.
points: Meeting any one route is enough.

POL-9.4.1-Q05.lead: 2% of 543 rounds up to 11 seats, from 3 states.
points: 4 seats goes with the 6%-in-4-states route.
22 would be about 4% of seats.

POL-9.4.1-Q06.lead: Route 1 needs 6% votes in 4 states plus 4 LS seats.
points: Vote share alone is not enough.
2 seats also fail the 2% (11 seats) route.
8% is a state-party condition, not national.

POL-9.4.1-Q07.lead: 6%+2 assembly; 6%+1 LS; 3%/3 seats; 1 per 25 LS seats.
points: The fifth condition is 8% of total valid votes, with no seat needed.

POL-9.4.1-Q08.lead: It is 3% of seats or 3 seats, whichever is more.
points: The 3% refers to seats, not votes.
2 seats is tied to 6% vote share.
A fraction of 25 also counts as one more seat; 26–50 seats would need 2.

POL-9.4.1-Q11.lead: A state party's symbol is reserved only in its state(s).
points: Reserved symbols are for recognised parties only.
Their travel costs are not added to the candidate's expenditure.

POL-9.4.1-Q14.lead: Independents and RUPP candidates need ten proposers.

head: Statement
Verdict
rows: A. One proposer for recognised party

points: Section 33 of the RP Act, 1951 sets this rule.

POL-9.4.1-Q15.lead: AAP broom, NPP book, CPI(M) hammer-sickle-star, BSP elephant.
points: BJP has the lotus and INC the hand.

POL-9.4.1-Q18.lead: BSP retained national status; AAP gained it.
points: ECI order dated 10 April 2023.
AAP's national status came in 2023, not 2022.

POL-9.4.1-Q19.lead: CPI corn-and-sickle, NCP clock, AITC flowers-and-grass.
points: CPI(M), still national, uses hammer, sickle and star.

POL-9.4.1-Q20.lead: P.A. Sangma founded the NPP in 2013.
points: Conrad Sangma, his son, now leads it.
P.K. Mahanta founded the AGP (1985).

POL-9.4.1-Q21.lead: In Assam, the elephant belongs to the AGP.

head: Statement
Verdict
rows: 1. TDP cycle reserved only where recognised

points: BSP uses the elephant everywhere except Assam.
SP also uses the cycle, but in other states.

POL-9.4.1-Q23.lead: Reservation is state-wise, so symbols can repeat across states.
points: Bow and arrow: Shiv Sena and JMM.
Two leaves: AIADMK and Kerala Congress.

POL-9.4.1-Q24.lead: Bow-arrow Shiv Sena/JMM; lion FB/MGP; two leaves AIADMK; car BRS.
points: BRS's party emblem is the Telangana map, but its election symbol is the car.

POL-9.4.1-Q25.lead: Recognition depends on poll performance and is reviewed.
points: So the number of national and state parties keeps changing.
Review after two elections means roughly every 10 years.

POL-9.4.1-Q26.lead: Para 15 empowers the ECI to decide splinter-group disputes.
points: Upheld in Sadiq Ali v ECI (1971).
Speaker decides disqualification, not symbol disputes.
Art 103 concerns MPs' disqualification.
POL-9.4.1-Q26.also: ECI gave Shiv Sena to the Shinde faction (2023) and NCP to the Ajit Pawar faction (2024).

POL-9.4.1-Q27.lead: Sadiq Ali (1971) upheld the Symbols Order and Para 15.
points: Mohinder Singh Gill: ECI's plenary powers under Art 324.
T.N. Seshan: multi-member ECI.
Anoop Baranwal (2023): appointment of ECs.

POL-9.4.1-Q28.lead: Para 16A allows suspension/withdrawal for MCC violation.
points: Para 15 covers splinter-group disputes.
Para 6A has state party conditions.
29A is a section of the RP Act on registration.

POL-9.4.1-Q29.lead: The drive affected only RUPPs, not recognised parties.
points: 334 delisted in August and 474 in September 2025.
AAP's national status came in April 2023.

POL-9.4.1-Q33.lead: Routes are alternatives; meeting one is enough.

head: Statement
Verdict
rows: A. State party in 4 states suffices

points: AAP got national status in 2023 through the four-state route.

POL-9.5.1-Q01.lead: Art 329A, on PM and Speaker elections, now stands repealed.
points: Part XV covers Arts 324-329.
Arts 324A, 326A and 328A do not exist in the Constitution.
POL-9.5.1-Q01.also: Art 329A was inserted by the 39th Amendment (1975) and later repealed.

POL-9.5.1-Q02.lead: Rajya Sabha is indirectly elected; statements 2 and 3 are correct.
points: Rajya Sabha members are elected by elected MLAs through proportional representation.
President and Vice-President have special electoral colleges.
Council seats include graduates', teachers' and local-body constituencies.

POL-9.5.1-Q03.lead: Art 325 lists only religion, race, caste and sex.
points: Residence is in fact a valid ground under Art 326 (non-residence).
Place of birth and descent appear in Art 16, not Art 325.
There is one general roll, ending separate communal electorates.

POL-9.5.1-Q04.lead: A common roll was adopted precisely to end separate electorates.
points: Art 325 provides one general roll per constituency.
Separate electorates were linked to communal division and Partition.
So R directly explains A.

POL-9.5.1-Q05.lead: Art 326 grounds: non-residence, unsound mind, crime, corrupt/illegal practice.
points: Literacy is not a qualification for voting in India.
Crime is also a listed ground.
Universal adult franchise needs no property or education test.

POL-9.5.1-Q06.lead: State law under Art 328 only fills gaps left by Parliament.
points: Art 327 gives Parliament the lead power over all election matters.
Art 328 applies only where Parliament has not made provision.
A state law can supplement, never override, Parliament's law.

POL-9.5.1-Q07.lead: Art 329(a) and the Delimitation Act bar court challenge.
points: Delimitation orders have the force of law.
Writ and Supreme Court routes are both barred for such orders.
Election petitions are for challenging an election result, not boundaries.

POL-9.5.1-Q08.lead: Any elector or candidate may file; HC tries, SC hears appeal.
points: Statement 1 is wrong: any elector of the constituency can also file.
Before 1966, election tribunals heard petitions.
A successful petition can lead to a fresh election.

POL-9.5.1-Q09.lead: Both true, but HCs decide because no tribunal was ever created.
points: Parliament has never set up an election tribunal under Art 323B.
L. Chandra Kumar struck down the ouster clause, a separate point.
Even if a tribunal were set up, appeals would go to the High Court.

POL-9.5.1-Q10.lead: Rules 1961, Symbols Order 1968, Pres/VP Act 1952, UT Act 1963.
points: The Delimitation Commission Act also dates from 1952.
The Symbols Order governs recognition of parties and allotment of symbols.
The CEC Conditions of Service Act is of 1991.
The District Collector usually acts as DEO.
RO and ERO are separate roles for the same constituency.
The Presiding Officer is helped by polling officers.

POL-9.5.1-Q13.lead: In UTs, the Returning Officer appoints them.
points: In states, the District Election Officer appoints them.
The CEO supervises at state/UT level but does not appoint booth staff.
The Lieutenant Governor has no role in poll staffing.

POL-9.5.1-Q14.lead: Observers are General, Expenditure and Police; there are no Judicial Observers.
points: General Observers watch every stage of the process.
Expenditure Observers monitor candidates' spending.
Police Observers are IPS officers watching law and order.
POL-9.5.1-Q14.also: Observers report directly to the Election Commission.

POL-9.5.1-Q15.lead: Assembly notification is in the Governor's name, not the CM's.
points: The roll is prepared and revised before any poll.
ECI issues notifications in the names of President and Governor.
The Chief Minister has no role in notifying elections.

POL-9.5.1-Q16.lead: The President may dissolve the Lok Sabha early in such a case.
points: Five years is the maximum, not a guaranteed, term.
ECI only conducts elections; it cannot dissolve a House.
Courts do not order general elections.

POL-9.5.1-Q17.lead: MCC applies from the schedule announcement, not notification.
points: The schedule is announced weeks before the formal notification.
MCC is not a statute; it rests on party consensus.
It aims at a level playing field for all contestants.

POL-9.5.1-Q18.lead: Nomination, scrutiny, withdrawal (within 2 days), then poll and counting.
points: Nominations are filed over about a week after notification.
The oath must be taken before the day of scrutiny.
Campaign and polling come after withdrawal; counting is last.

POL-9.5.1-Q19.lead: Withdrawal is allowed within two days after scrutiny.
points: About one week is the window for filing nominations.
48 hours before the poll is when campaigning stops.
The Returning Officer scrutinises nominations and may reject defective ones.

POL-9.5.1-Q20.lead: Oath is taken in person, latest the day before scrutiny.
points: It is normally made right after filing the nomination.
It is administered by the RO/ARO or an authorised officer.
Polling-day and withdrawal-day deadlines are wrong.

POL-9.5.1-Q21.lead: Both are true, but campaign length does not explain the silence period.
points: The 48-hour silence lets voters decide without pressure.
The two-week minimum is a separate rule on campaign length.
So R does not explain A.

POL-9.5.1-Q22.lead: Ballots use the languages ECI specifies, not English alone.
points: Names appear in English and the regional language or Hindi.
Each candidate's allotted symbol is printed beside the name.
Free symbols go to independents and unrecognised parties.

POL-9.5.1-Q23.lead: Phasing is for deploying security forces, not due to FPTP.
points: Staggered polling lets forces and monitors move constituency to constituency.
FPTP is the counting rule; it does not need phased polling.
Both statements are true independently.

POL-9.5.1-Q24.lead: ECI cut the limit from 1,500 to 1,200 electors in 2025.
points: 1,500 was the older limit still printed in some books.
Polling stations should be within about 2 km of voters.
Each station stays open at least 8 hours.
POL-9.5.1-Q24.also: Bihar became the first state with all booths under 1,200 voters.

POL-9.5.1-Q25.lead: All three are standard polling norms.
points: Voting is by secret ballot, often in schools or community halls.
Name is checked on the roll and ID verified before inking.
The vote is cast on the control unit with the presiding officer's help.

POL-9.5.1-Q26.lead: Exit polls may be released half an hour after the final phase ends.
points: Per-phase release would influence later phases.
Opinion polls are barred from 48 hours before polling till its close.
Waiting until counting is not required.

POL-9.5.1-Q27.lead: Under FPTP, the candidate with most votes wins without a majority.
points: Run-offs are not part of India's system.
Preference counting applies to STV elections like Rajya Sabha and President.
The RO, not the ECI, declares the result and issues the certificate.

POL-9.5.1-Q28.lead: ECI notifies the list of elected members; the President then summons the House.
points: The President summons, but does not constitute, the House.
The pro tem Speaker only administers oaths.
The Law Ministry has no role in constituting the House.

POL-9.5.1-Q29.lead: Courts do not interfere mid-process; ECI decides until results.
points: After results, the remedy is an election petition in the High Court.
Art 329(b) bars other routes of challenge.
The Governor has no role in election disputes.

POL-9.5.1-Q30.lead: Assembly and Council candidates pay Rs 10,000; SC/ST Rs 5,000.
points: Rs 25,000 and Rs 12,500 apply to Lok Sabha.
Rs 5,000/2,500 was the pre-2009 assembly amount.
OBC candidates pay the general rate.
Section 33(7) of the RP Act sets the two-seat limit.
Before 1996 there was no such limit.
Goswami Committee wanted contest from two seats ended.

POL-9.5.1-Q32.lead: One elector of the constituency is enough for a recognised-party candidate.
points: Independents and unrecognised-party candidates need ten proposers.
The proposer must be an elector of that constituency.
The same rule applies to Assembly elections.
Simultaneous polls share costs between Centre and state.
Accounts are lodged with the District Election Officer under RP Act s.78.
Failure to file can lead to disqualification by ECI.

POL-9.5.1-Q34.lead: JPC-multi-member, Tarkunde-no retirees, Goswami-aid in kind, Vohra-crime.
points: Tarkunde Committee was set up by Jayaprakash Narayan for Citizens for Democracy.
Tarkunde also wanted EC members to have SC-judge-level qualifications.
Goswami was Law Minister in the V.P. Singh government.

POL-9.5.1-Q35.lead: JP set it up on behalf of Citizens for Democracy.
points: It was a non-official committee, not a government body.
It wanted a three-member, independent ECI.
The Law Commission's 170th report (1999) was a separate exercise.

POL-9.5.1-Q36.lead: 1998 replacement began, 2003 all state polls, 2004 Lok Sabha.
points: Over 10 lakh EVMs were used in 2004 across all 543 seats.
The 2004 poll was the 14th Lok Sabha election.
Some books misprint 563 seats for 2004; the correct figure is 543.

POL-9.5.1-Q37.lead: EVMs eliminate invalid votes; statement 3 is wrong.
points: BEL is in Bengaluru and ECIL in Hyderabad, both PSUs.
Braille signage came in 2018.
EVMs also speed up counting and save paper.
The slip shows the candidate's name and symbol for about seven seconds.
All EVMs were paired with VVPATs from the 2019 Lok Sabha poll.
PUCL (2013) is the NOTA case, not VVPAT.

POL-9.5.1-Q39.lead: Both true; the origin of NOTA does not explain its no-effect rule.
points: NOTA votes are counted but have no effect on the result.
It was first used in Dec 2013 in Delhi, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh and MP.
The court linked the right to reject to freedom of expression.
ENCORE stands for Enabling Communication on Real-time Environment.
Suvidha also handles rally and vehicle permissions.
cVIGIL is the app for reporting MCC violations.

POL-9.5.1-Q41.lead: The age limit was raised from 80 to 85 in March 2024.
points: Postal ballot for absentee voters aged 80+ was introduced in 2019; ECI's home-voting drive was used in the 2023 Karnataka poll.
Persons with benchmark disabilities (40%+) are also eligible.
Service voters and election-duty staff use postal ballots too.

POL-9.5.1-Q43.lead: Summary revision updates the roll without field visits.
points: Intensive revision prepares a fresh roll by door-to-door enumeration.
Special intensive revision is a fresh, comprehensive roll exercise.
Partly intensive mixes field checks with the existing roll.

POL-9.5.1-Q44.lead: Sen first, Sundaram longest, Peri Sastri first Telugu, Ramadevi first woman.
points: Sukumar Sen conducted the first general election of 1951-52.
K.V.K. Sundaram served 1958-1967.
V.S. Ramadevi, also Telugu, held the post briefly in 1990.

POL-9.5.1-Q45.lead: Periodic delimitation restores vote-value parity as population shifts.
points: Delimitation fixes boundaries of territorial constituencies.
It is done by the Delimitation (Boundary) Commission.
R is the core reason behind A.

POL-9.5.1-Q46.lead: It is statutory, and Houses cannot modify its orders.
points: It is set up by the Centre under a Delimitation Act of Parliament.
Its orders have the force of law and cannot be challenged in court.
Orders are laid before Lok Sabha/Assembly only for information.

POL-9.5.1-Q48.lead: Art 324 deals with the Election Commission, not delimitation or seat reservation.
points: Art 82 provides readjustment of Lok Sabha seats after every census.
Art 170 covers Assembly composition and readjustment.
Arts 330 and 332 reserve seats for SC/ST in Lok Sabha and Assemblies.

POL-9.5.1-Q49.lead: The 87th Amendment changed boundaries, not seat numbers.
points: Seat totals still rest on the 1971 census.
The 87th Amendment made 2001 census the basis for redrawing boundaries.
SC/ST reserved seats were re-worked on the 2001 census.

POL-9.5.1-Q50.lead: The freeze was a population-control incentive.
points: Without the freeze, southern states would have lost seat share.
The freeze was meant to run till 2000, later extended.
R correctly explains A.

POL-9.5.1-Q51.lead: Seat totals 1971; boundaries and SC/ST 2001; J&K 2011.
points: Within a state, constituencies are made roughly equal in population (2001).
J&K used 2011 because population had more than doubled since 1981.
Boundaries too are frozen until the first census after 2026.

POL-9.5.1-Q52.lead: Associate members could neither vote nor sign orders.
points: Members: SC judge (chair), CEC or EC nominee, State Election Commissioner.
Each state had 10 associate members: 5 MPs and 5 MLAs.
Associates were nominated by the respective Speakers.

POL-9.5.1-Q53.lead: Jharkhand's order was nullified; four NE states were deferred.
points: Deferred: Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Nagaland.
Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram got new boundaries.
The 2009 poll used new boundaries in 499 of 543 seats.

POL-9.5.1-Q54.lead: NE states were removed from its purview in March 2021.
points: It then worked only on the UT of J&K.
Its final order came in May 2022.
Its report: 'Delimited Landscape of Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir'.
Earlier the state Assembly had 111 seats, incl. 24 PoJK and 4 Ladakh (87 filled).
Excluding Ladakh, J&K seats rose from 83 to 90, a gain of 7.
The LG may nominate 2 women members.

POL-9.5.1-Q56.lead: Jammu has 43 and Kashmir 47 seats, so statement 1 is wrong.
points: ST seats: 6 in Jammu, 3 in Kashmir; SC seats: 7.
J&K was treated as one unit, giving 5 x 18 = 90.
Anantnag-Rajouri PC joins areas of both regions.

POL-9.5.1-Q57.lead: The migrant recommendations are separate from the binding order.
points: Migrant members were to have powers like Puducherry's nominated members.
PoJK displaced persons may get representation by nomination.
Both bodies have Law and Justice as nodal ministry.

POL-9.5.1-Q58.lead: It got 298 votes for and 230 against, below two-thirds.
points: Art 368 needs two-thirds of members present and voting.
The companion Delimitation Bill 2026 was withdrawn the same day.
The freeze till the first census after 2026 continues.
POL-9.5.1-Q58.also: Southern states, including Andhra Pradesh, feared losing seat share.

POL-9.5.2-Q01.lead: Art 171 fixes Council size; details left to Parliament's law.
points: Art 81 covers Lok Sabha composition.
Art 170 covers Legislative Assembly composition.
Art 168 only creates state legislatures.

POL-9.5.2-Q02.lead: The Constitution only outlines; Parliament filled details by law.
points: The gap left by Arts 81, 170, 171 is why the two RPAs were enacted.
R directly gives the reason for A.

POL-9.5.2-Q03.lead: RPA 1950 builds map and rolls; RPA 1951 runs the contest.
points: RPA 1950 does not conduct elections at all.
Corrupt practices are defined in Sec 123 of the 1951 Act.

POL-9.5.2-Q04.lead: RPA 1950 gives the President this power after ECI consultation.
points: ECI is only consulted, not the decider here.
State Election Commissions deal with local bodies, not Assembly seats.
POL-9.5.2-Q04.also: Major delimitations are done by Delimitation Commissions under separate Acts.

POL-9.5.2-Q05.lead: Election disputes belong to RPA 1951, not RPA 1950.
points: CEO/DEO/ERO, UT Rajya Sabha seats and civil-court bar are all in RPA 1950.
Civil-court bar is common to both Acts.

POL-9.5.2-Q06.lead: Voter side is 1950 Act; candidate side is 1951 Act.
points: Mixing voter and candidate qualifications is the usual trap.

POL-9.5.2-Q07.lead: 1 Jan, 1 Apr, 1 Jul and 1 Oct are qualifying dates now.
points: Earlier only 1 January was the qualifying date.
A youth turning 18 need not wait a full year to enrol.

POL-9.5.2-Q08.lead: Aadhaar linking is voluntary; 'spouse' made the law gender-neutral.
points: No one can be denied enrolment for not giving Aadhaar.
Female service personnel's husbands can now vote as service voters.

POL-9.5.2-Q09.lead: Art 328 power is subject to Parliament's law under Art 327.
points: Art 327 is Parliament's power, not the state's.
ECI cannot decide which law is valid.

POL-9.5.2-Q10.lead: Delimitation is under RPA 1950 and Delimitation Acts.
points: Nine stages run from nomination to election expenses.
Assets declaration and multiple elections are both stages.

POL-9.5.2-Q11.lead: He must vacate all but one seat.
points: One person cannot represent two constituencies.
Since 1996, Sec 33(7) allows contesting from at most two seats.

POL-9.5.2-Q13.lead: Lower Houses 25 years; Upper Houses 30 years.
points: Voting age is 18 (61st CAA); do not confuse with candidature age.

POL-9.5.2-Q14.lead: Oath before ECI-authorised person is required; being an elector is mandatory.
points: Candidate must be an Indian citizen and a registered elector.
Oath form is given in the Third Schedule of the Constitution.

POL-9.5.2-Q15.lead: Domicile removal was upheld, not struck down.
points: Kuldip Nayar also upheld open ballot for Rajya Sabha elections.

POL-9.5.2-Q16.lead: Independent/unrecognised party candidates need ten proposers (Sec 33).
points: One proposer suffices for a recognised party candidate.
Fifty proposers is a Presidential election requirement.

POL-9.5.2-Q17.lead: Arts 102/191 list disqualifications and let Parliament add more.
points: Arts 84/173 give qualifications.
Arts 101/190 deal with vacation of seats.
Arts 99/188 deal with oath.
POL-9.5.2-Q17.also: RPA 1951 Sections 8-11 are that 'law of Parliament'.

POL-9.5.2-Q18.lead: Sentence of 2+ years: disqualified during it plus 6 years.
points: 5 years applies to dismissal for corruption (Sec 9).
Only-during-jail ignores the extra 6 years.

POL-9.5.2-Q19.lead: Sec 8(2) threshold is 6 months, not 6 years.
points: Sec 8(1) offences: disqualified 6 years from conviction even if only fined.
Sec 8(3) is the general 2-year rule.

POL-9.5.2-Q20.lead: Lily Thomas made disqualification immediate on conviction.
points: PUCL (2013) gave NOTA.
Kuldip Nayar was on Rajya Sabha domicile.
Anoop Baranwal was on ECI appointments.

POL-9.5.2-Q21.lead: President decides on ECI's opinion; maximum 6 years.
points: The High Court only finds the corrupt practice in the petition.
Speaker decides defection cases, not this.

POL-9.5.2-Q22.lead: Sec 9 disqualifies for 5 years from dismissal.
points: 3 years is for failure to lodge expense accounts.
6 years is linked to conviction rules.
Sec 11 removes or reduces a disqualification; it does not add one.

POL-9.5.2-Q24.lead: Sec 10A applies to every contesting candidate, winner or loser.
points: The disqualification is for 3 years, not life.
It is ECI's order, not a court fine.
POL-9.5.2-Q24.also: Accounts are lodged with the District Election Officer within 30 days.
